answer: The gale multiplier is published, charged in knoll, and lagoon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2842 identities would post 3796 proofs and burn roughly 49 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
